arguments.change_summary: Probe: set new step content on TC-54484 to determine which field edit_test_case_v1 reads steps from and where they land on read-back (decisive experiment vs create_test_case_v1 finding); also resend priority=318618 unchanged to check echo of upper-block option id.

contract.json_path: /test_case/<field> per field (e.g. /test_case/name, /test_case/test_case_steps) — but this is a per-field wrapper notation only. The body must be sent FLAT; a literal nested `test_case` object is rejected client-side with 'unknown body: test_case'. Confirmed accurate (see attempts[0]).

notes:
DECISIVE EXPERIMENT (steps field, in vs out): the request body field that actually carries steps into edit_test_case_v1 is `test_case_steps` (flat, array of {step, result, order, ...}) — exactly the same field name as create_test_case_v1. Sending it (with `template_step_type: "test_case_steps"` alongside it, per the contract's own warning that template defaults to test_case_text otherwise) landed the new step content. On read-back, the content comes back in `test_case_steps` (an ARRAY of step objects), while the OTHER declared field `test_case.steps` came back as `[]` (empty) both immediately in the edit response and on an independent GET afterward. This is CONSISTENT with the create_test_case_v1 finding: `test_case_steps` is the only field that round-trips step content on both create and edit; `steps` is dead on both paths. NEW drift found here that create_test_case_v1's probe did not surface: edit_test_case_v1's declared 200 schema types `test_case.test_case_steps` as a single OBJECT (with properties background/feature/hashed_id/order/result/scenario/step/... at the top level), but the actual field is always an ARRAY of such objects — a real type mismatch, not just an empty-vs-populated difference.

PARTIAL-UPDATE SEMANTICS (PUT vs PATCH): for ordinary content fields, edit_test_case_v1 behaves as a genuine PARTIAL MERGE (PATCH-like), not a destructive full replace. Evidence: setup step 3 sent ONLY `{name: ...}`, omitting steps/priority/case_type/status/tags entirely, and setup step 4's independent read-back confirms priority (318618/Medium), case_type (318626/Other), status (318632/Active), tags (['mcp-probe']), and the steps set in the prior edit all SURVIVED unchanged. This contradicts the naive inference from the existence of an `edit_test_case_partial_v1` sibling that this path must be a destructive full replace — for the fields tested, it is not.

HOWEVER, there IS a real, undeclared, destructive side effect worth flagging: `template_id` and `template_name` get reset to `null`, and `template`/`template_step_type` silently revert to `test_case_text`, on ANY edit call that does not explicitly resend `template_id` — even when the edit is about a completely unrelated field like `name`. This is a real persisted change (confirmed via an independent GET after the edit, not just an artifact of the edit response), even though the underlying `test_case_steps` row data itself is NOT deleted (it is still returned in full on the next read) — only the template/step-shape classification is silently downgraded. This is more specific than the contract's own warning ('template defaults to test_case_text when omitted, which discards test_case_steps you sent') — the discarding claim is partly wrong: the step records survive, but the template metadata does not. Recommend the contract explicitly say 'omitting `template_id`/`template_step_type` on ANY edit call resets the case's template classification to test_case_text, independent of which fields you are actually editing' rather than framing it only as a steps-discarding risk.

One more response-shape wrinkle: `history_count`, `test_run_results_count` and `test_run_results_issues_count` came back as `null` in the edit response itself (setup step 3) but as real integers (3, 0, 0) on the very next independent GET (setup step 4) — a transient/eventually-consistent rendering quirk of the edit response specifically, not real data loss. Worth noting so nobody reads a null count in an edit response as the count having been wiped.

WRAPPER TRAP: contract guidance for edit_test_case_v1 explicitly and correctly states the body must be FLAT — sending a nested `test_case` object is rejected client-side before any HTTP call, verbatim: 'unknown body: test_case ... test_case is a wrapper this surface builds for you from each field's json_path — send the fields directly instead of nesting them'. Confirmed exactly as declared (attempts[0]). This is the OPPOSITE of create_test_case_v1 (where nested was required) and MATCHES create_test_plan_v1 (flat required) — no drift on this point for edit_test_case_v1.

OTHER OBSERVATIONS: priority id 318618 was resent unchanged in the decisive-experiment edit and echoed back correctly as {id:318618, internal_name:'medium', name:'Medium'} confirming the upper-block option ids are live on this path too. `field_name` is declared on priority/case_type/status option objects in edit_test_case_v1's response schema, but is ABSENT from the actual edit response for all three (confirmed twice, across both successful edits) — yet the SAME fields DO carry `field_name` when read via get_test_case_by_integer_id_v1 (baseline and final read-back both have it). So this is an edit-response-specific omission, not a general absence. Undeclared `value_category` appears on case_type/priority/status/automation_state option objects in the edit response, exactly as flagged as a risk in the task brief (null for the first three, 'manual' for automation_state) — none of these are mentioned in the declared schema.
